record.original_question: Suppose that f is a plane K-quasiconformal mapping of the unit disc D onto itself. Show that there exists a finite constant b = b(K) such that m(f (E)) ≤ b{m(E)}1/K for each measurable set E ⊂ D. Here m denotes plane Lebesgue measure. Such an inequality is known (see [303]) with the exponent K replaced by a constant a = a(K). (F. W. Gehring)

evidence.quote: Suppose that f is a plane K-quasiconformal mapping of the unit disc D onto itself. Show that there exists a finite constant b = b(K) such that m(f (E)) ≤ b{m(E)}1/K for each measurable set E ⊂ D.
This has been proved by Astala [33]. His proof has been substantially simplified by Eremenko and Hamilton [244].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc, and let $m$ denote planar Lebesgue measure. A homeomorphism $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{D}$ is called $K$-quasiconformal (for some $K\ge 1$) if $f$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{D})$ and its complex (Beltrami) dilatation $\mu_f=\partial_{\bar z}f/\partial_z f$ satisfies $\|\mu_f\|_\infty \le (K-1)/(K+1)$ almost everywhere.

Prove that there exists a finite constant $b=b(K)$, depending only on $K$, such that for every $K$-quasiconformal mapping $f$ of $\mathbb{D}$ onto itself and every Lebesgue-measurable set $E\subset \mathbb{D}$,
$$m\bigl(f(E)\bigr) \le b\,\bigl(m(E)\bigr)^{1/K}.$$
The exponent $1/K$ is the sharp one; in particular, prove that the inequality holds with exponent $1/K$ (not merely with some smaller exponent $a(K)$).
artifact.status_search_result: This is Gehring's area distortion conjecture for planar quasiconformal mappings. It was proved by K. Astala (Acta Math. 173 (1994), 37–60), who established the sharp area distortion inequality with exponent 1/K. A simplified proof was later given by Eremenko and Hamilton.

status_evidence.title: Area distortion of quasiconformal mappings
status_evidence.snippet: K. Astala, Area distortion of quasiconformal mappings, Acta Mathematica 173 (1994), 37-60, proves the sharp area distortion inequality with exponent 1/K.
status_evidence.claim: Astala proved the sharp area distortion inequality with exponent 1/K, settling Gehring's conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On the area distortion by quasiconformal mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Eremenko and Hamilton give a simplified proof of Astala's area distortion theorem.
status_evidence.claim: A simplified proof was provided by Eremenko and Hamilton.
